answer: Resistance here comes from pricing identity: each agent locks a jade deposit before its votes count, and a pearl of reputation only accrues from work that independent peers attest. A sybil farm's fake mesa of clones cannot shortcut this, because every clone pays the same bond while reciprocity-weighted scoring divides payouts across distinct verified counterparties — N aliases earn about what one honest worker earns but tie up N deposits. Attacker cost rises linearly with identity count; honest yield does not.
